summary: Cascaden Tower on Windy Lake near Sudbury, built about 1928, closed in 1972 and cut down by the MNRF in July 2024.

facts.design: Light steel tower with an octagon cab
facts.status_note: Cut down by the Ministry of Natural Resources and Forestry in July 2024; debris removed by helicopter.
facts.agency: Ministry of Natural Resources and Forestry

events.note: Clayton Self recalls a 1928 tower; the Canada Lookouts entry gives 1928 for the erection. The Star says late 1920s or early 1930s.
Photo caption places Jack Naylor at his map table in the tower, circa 1942.
Department of Lands and Forests report: about 13 1/2 miles of telephone line built between Cartier and the tower.
Ron Greig, quoted by the Star, says the tower closed in 1972 after Naylor's long service.
Ministry says work began July 8; the tower was cut down and debris removed by helicopter.

corrections.why: The Star reports the Ministry of Natural Resources and Forestry cut the tower down in July 2024, so the brief's unknown status is out of date.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Star says late 1920s or early 1930s, but Clayton Self recalls 1928 and the Canada Lookouts entry gives 1928. The story uses 1928 and gives the Star's broader range.
The 2018 Accent article spells the fire warden's name Nyler; the 2024 article spells it Naylor. The story uses Naylor.

sources.title: Fire tower at Windy Lake no longer stands

notes_for_editor: The 2024 Sudbury Star article (James Moodie) is the key source: it reports the July 2024 removal and quotes the MNRF statement. The firelookout.ca record and geohub dataset page returned no details beyond location. The Star calls it the Cascaden Tower after the township. Height 80-foot is the Star's wording, converted to metres here. Access today is not described in any source; the 2018 article describes a gated camp road. Ron Greig is quoted through the Star and the 2018 Accent article, which spell his name differently in places. Brief status 'unknown' corrected to removed. No photo added: the Star's 2019 photo has no direct image URL in the fetched text.
